leads.author: MrNobody; Denis Golovkin; Sparky; 3.1415926535897932384626
leads.claim: The dbbi 'yellow/blue primes' rail (b/be tokens at prime positions) equals the LSB of each byte of the first-image grid, i.e. the parity of the ASCII chars of 'gsmg.io/theseedisplanted' = 111101110011110110010010 (0xf73d92). About the first 20 bits match exactly. The tail needs a 'fix', and three different fixes are proposed: (a) count the near-white FEFEFE cell as blue -> all 23 primes match (Sparky); Denis says one RGB channel's LSB bit-plane already shows that cell as blue (channel not stated); (b) 0xf73d92>>1 = 0x7b9ec9, +3 ('trinity') = 0x7b9ecc (Denis); (c) set index 21 of the creator's {1},{4},{21} -> 23-bit mask 11110111001111011001101 = 0x7b9ecd (MrNobody). 3.1415 claims 24 bits match; Denis: dbbi holds at most 84 logical indices.
leads.reaction_rebuttal: 👑: {1},{4},{21} is an April-Fools date, not a board correction. Whore Amazing: dead end; counting 'be' as one token is ad hoc; never produced readable text. Sparky/Denis: shuffle Monte-Carlo says the alignment is not chance (agrees with our earlier 0/5000 shuffles). Open: what consumes the rail.
leads.local_check: URL parity string reproduced exactly (= 0xf73d92). The comparison of the rail's last bits against the mask was not re-run.

leads.author: MrNobody; sniper; Coinionaire; nieods
leads.claim: Both small OpenSSL objects are 'Salted__' + 8-byte salt + 80-byte ciphertext (5 AES blocks): the SalPhaseIon inline blob (salt 3ab585348552415d) and the Phase 3.2 tail 'keyhole' blob (salt b45a5e3d827593ca). Under AES-CBC with PKCS7 padding the plaintext must be 64..79 bytes. Cosmic Duality ciphertext = 1328 bytes. There is no separate IV; key and IV both come from the salt.
leads.reaction_rebuttal: Naddiseo challenged 'exactly 64 lowercase hex'; MrNobody corrected it to 64-79 bytes. Our arithmetic: a bare WIF (51-52 chars, even with a trailing newline) would encrypt to 64 bytes, not 80. That rules out nieods' expectation that the 3.2.2 blob holds the base58 WIF. Plaintexts that do fit: 64-hex (+newline), or 2x32 raw bytes + up to 15 bytes.
leads.local_check: Confirmed: small ct 80, inner ct 80, cosmic ct 1328 (salt 2d3f6fe06dc950e6).

leads.author: The Boss Jimmy; Coinionaire; TekniskTrading; gemboi; The Bee-llionaire
leads.claim: An LLM-built 'chain' is circulating: Cosmic Duality 'decrypts' to 1327 bytes (SHA256 4f7a1e4efe4bf6c5581e32505c019657cb7b030e90232d33f011aca6a5e9c081). A nested 'Chain4' gives 1151 bytes (SHA256 e4269ed5fbb202a81e5e1aa6b5190fdd1ea126b2c8547ea7cdbdf45387ea135b). Small blob B1 gives 79 bytes split 32+32+15 (tail 38d4f4c90cb45fdfc8cff50d0ed1c5), read as 'Half'/'Better Half' keys -> addresses 1JG648yaB7Wp2dpUfcZoRSD4q35oq47vCu and 145ZQ9siLrsXBKf465wjdyQYAP5dRwhRhQ. An 'XOR triangle' needs an operand 'cosmic_A'/'cc' (sha256 prefix cd3fea3d). '103x103 route' invariants: S=5193, Wr=268603, Wc=268828, p_big=58, p_little=46. The passwords were never published.
leads.reaction_rebuttal: Boss Jimmy himself calls the keys 'unauthenticated' and cosmic_A a 'phantom' (first mention: a March-2026 issue from a brand-new account; no bytes in 22 forks or archived pages). ΞZ: 'chain4 was llm nonsense'. 'Me' (#68747): cosmic_A.bin doesn't exist. Our arithmetic: 1328->1327 and 80->79 are exactly PKCS7 pad=0x01, which a wrong key produces with p~1/256. Any 32 random bytes is a valid secp256k1 key. So none of these outputs proves itself; treat them as padding false positives unless someone shows readable plaintext.

leads.author: X; Loupi; Flo Sku; Thiago Santos; Suppa; n04oh
leads.claim: btcseed: deduplicate dbbi into the keyword 'dbifhceg(a)', build a 5x5 Bifid square (no j), and Bifid-decrypt all 570 faed letters as one period. The 570-char output starts 'btcseeddeoemckeadhbschdkbdcsdkdv...' (SHA256 15d62c8228c1a30f3f6280fcdce2251fe616135e9de291b0c7b8a792dd8d0507). Over 3000 faed shuffles: mean #z 2.89, P(#z>=1)=95.8%, P(#z==1)=14.2%, so the z and the b/c/d/e alternation are mechanical. Suppa: P('btcseed' named in advance)~1/4M; ~1/100k after look-elsewhere (40 of 23,881 seven-letter words fit the pattern). Sparky/B58/👑: coincidence. Asked 'what about btcseed?' on 2026-09-01, the creator did not reply. Cycle-37 verdict stands: probably coincidence.
leads.local_check: Reproduced with scratch/bifid.py: starts 'btcseeddeoem', sha256[:8]=15d62c82, one z at index 97, even positions only {b,c,d,e}.

Left and right are each white noise, but L-R carries a periodic signal: period exactly 684 samples at 44.1 kHz (64.47 Hz), odd harmonics only, half-wave antisymmetric (avg[k] = -avg[k+342], corr 0.9997).
